speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the recent camping trip in Minnesota and your history of self-resolving knee pain are significant clues. Given your age and symptoms, do you know if you have had a tick bite during your camping trip, and can you describe the specific appearance and distribution of your skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) with arthralgia. The classic "slapped cheek" rash is absent, but the violaceous lacy reticular rash on the wrists/hands combined with acute symmetric arthritis/arthralgia in a young patient is highly characteristic, often preceded by a mild flu-like illness. The severe wrist swelling and tenderness you described are consistent with the reactive arthritis associated with Parvovirus B19 infection.
